main_text.p: de Me bene loqui, & Deum blasphema-re: adeo haec inter se invicem pugna-re videbantur, in me Fides, & in Deum Religio.

Erant tamen (laus Deo) ex mea par-te complures,docti pariter & pii, (idque multis parasangis ultra vulgarem illam Magnitudinem & mensuram scientiæ, quâ nonnulli ita gloriantur) quibus tàm integre probatur Victa[?] Causa, ut mecum pati potius vellent, quam in malis de-ferere.

Haud interim mirandum, si tot pii prætextus contra Me usurpati, homines alioqui non malos vehementer percel-lerent, & in partem adversam simul tra-herent: accedente præterea populari Concionatorum facundiâ, quibus nullum erat flagitium pro Deo mentiri, (vel quod ipsi Dei Causam appellare libuerat) diris omnibus devoventes, qui secum pari-ter devovere noluerant, & tam vehe-menter plaudentes Bono Fini, & in eum ita unicè intenti, ut nec, quàm illicita essent media, attenderent, nec in sceleris pro-fundum (quod revera Finis erat præ-cipuus) omnino penetrarent.
Homines imbecilli judicio, qui quod illis hic deeft, clamore improbo, & fe-dulitate farciunt, quorum magna pars Religionis, Me & Meos infamare, ut, qui

page.notes: Running head and title are in Greek capitals; the final letter is Greek eta, printed like H. A small black mark (ornament or stain) stands to the right of "Religio."; two dots stand on the line after "ferere."; neither is printed text and both are left out. "Victa" is doubtful: the scan shows a letter like "ct" or "ta" after "Vi"; marked [?]. "hic" in "illis hic deeft" is faint, read as plain "hic". "deeft" is a printing error and is kept as printed. "complures,docti" has no space after the comma as printed. The catchword "alias" stands alone at the bottom right and is not repeated in the text.
